subject: Private GPU pool stabilization and controlled ramp plan
messages:

Subject: Capacity gating + ramp cadence for private GPU pool (Nimbus)

Hi Marissa,

Quick context: we're finalizing our private deployment timetable for Nimbus' inference staging. We want a controlled, observable ramp rather than turning on full traffic at once. Two asks from our side:

1) Can Redwood propose a stabilization window strategy (how long to hold at each run-rate, expected cache warm times, recommended warm-pool sizes)?
2) Network/egress checklist — we need explicit max sustained egress numbers so our CISO can greenlight the subnet peering.

Target goal: get us to a steady-state of ~450 RPS (short-completion median) across the 24x7 baseline within four weeks of cutover, with ability to absorb short bursts to ~1.8k RPS for up to 5 minutes. We want P99 latency < 300ms for baseline traffic if possible (we understand burst behavior will differ).

We're flexible on the exact cadence but would appreciate a short playbook we can sign off on. Attaching our internal infra runbook if helpful.

Thanks,
Katie Ho
Head of Platform 
Nimbus Analytics

Katie — thanks for the clear goals. High level proposal below, attaching the ramp math and a compact warm-pool playbook. Please review and flag anything that must change for Nimbus' compliance window.

Summary proposal (short):
- Baseline target: 450 RPS sustained across the private fleet (24 GPU nodes initially).
- Warm-pool sizing: maintain 4 warm nodes (preloaded KV and common prefixes) to absorb sub-second scale-ups; warm fill time ~ 90s for typical prompt distribution.
- Stabilization windows: step-ups at 3x, 6x, 12x of baseline held for 24h / 72h / 7d respectively. Example: 450 RPS -> 1.35k RPS (24h) -> 2.7k RPS (72h) -> 5.4k RPS (7d) while monitoring error budget and p99 latency.
- Burst containment: short bursts up to 1.8k RPS for <= 5 minutes without autoscale; anything beyond triggers controlled admission and graceful degradation to model-quantized variant.
- KPIs and telemetry: token-level cost, p50/p95/p99 latency, queue depth, CPU/GPU utilization, cache hit ratio.

Notes:
- The 24-node starting point is conservative; math in the sheet shows equivalent configurations using 20xA100-80GB or 40xA10s depending on model and quantization.
- Network egress: plan for 1.2 Gbps sustained and 4 Gbps bursting headroom per region during the 2.7k RPS phase. Exact numbers in attachment.

Action items I'm proposing:
1) Nimbus sign-off on the stabilization windows and initial warm-pool count.
2) Redwood infra run an ingress/egress smoke test during the first 24h of each step.
3) A joint ops war room for the two 24h transitions (1.35k and 2.7k).

Attaching: ramp-math.xlsx, warm-pool-playbook.md, network-egress-checklist.pdf

—
Marissa Cole

Marissa — annotating with engineering constraints and a low-risk roll pattern.

On Tue, Aug 25, 2026 at 11:03 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Katie — thanks for the clear goals. High level proposal below, attaching the ramp math and a compact warm-pool playbook.

A few important details to lock down:
- Admission control: we'll gate at request-token thresholds not raw RPS for model-size fairness. For example, 450 RPS with average prompt size 120 tokens corresponds to ~54k tokens/sec sustained. We'll use token-based throttles and per-client weightings during ramp.
- Cache warm pattern: we recommend a two-hour synthetic warm-up window before ramp events: run sampled production prefixes (we can share a scrubbed prefix set) to fill KV and ONNX caches. This reduces p99 spike risk.
- Autoscale warm-up: our autoscaler requires ~90–120s to add a GPU instance and stabilize weights; rely on warm-pool to absorb the initial delta.
- Failure mode: if p99 exceeds 500ms for > 3 consecutive minutes during a step window, trigger automatic rollback to previous step and open the incident channel.

Proposed telemetry thresholds for go/no-go at each window (examples):
- Go: p99 < 350ms, error rate < 0.5%, GPU util < 85%
- Warn: p99 350–500ms OR error rate 0.5–1%
- Abort/rollback: p99 > 500ms OR error rate > 1% for > 3m

I'll prepare a short runbook for the war room that lists the metric panels, escalation numbers, and who toggles admission control.

—Jonas

Looping in support notes from CS/ops side. Practical items to confirm:
- On-call coverage: Redwood will provide primary on-call for first 72 hours of each step and standby for the remaining hold period. We'll map contacts in the war room doc.
- Cost guardrails: set a soft limit at +25% spend vs forecast for the first week of 2.7k step; notify both teams and pause auto-burst beyond warm-pool if exceeded.
- Contract ask: Nimbus to agree to the mutual action plan milestones (we'll provide a short DocuSign for the ramp commitments).

Also: recommend Nimbus enable request-tagging (client_id) so we can attribute hot prefixes to specific services during warmups. Small instrumentation helps reduce warm-pool churn.
